230	## Judgment and authority
231	
232	The [frame authority law](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-006-authority-conservation)
233	owns authority conservation for frame evaluation. Within a_c,
234	[AC-014](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-014-judgment-separation) owns its calculus
235	judgment separation. Where a consumer has adopted the construction engagement
236	profile and lawfully activated the applicable engagement,
237	[the Baseline](STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#complete-engagement-transition)
238	owns its exact Reviewer/Executive application of the detailed laws. Other
239	domain judgment and control functions retain their own declared contracts. Definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims
240	have distinct standing. A judgment binds a predicate, exact subject, basis,
241	evidence, assessor and any required independence. An operation grant permits
242	specified effects; decision authority retains its separately bound mandate.
243	Neither evidence shape nor actor capability
244	mints a grant. In a consumer-adopted, lawfully activated Baseline engagement, Baseline
245	Reviewer and Executive retain their exact roles from that profile. This account
246	assigns neither role or its authority. Domain control such as ODD next-action
247	selection remains with its own named function; the explanation appoints none.
248	
249	Unknown applicability, missing context, incompatible basis and failed predicates
250	remain observable. Severity grades the supported consequence if a finding manifests. Priority,
251	disposition, selected action and promotion effect remain distinct; their
252	assignment follows the applicable mandate. The semantic result remains separate
253	from the authoritative construction disposition, whose domain conditions belong
254	to [Spec's proportional disposition](SPEC_METHOD.md#proportional-disposition).
255	
256	[Construction assurance](#construction-assurance) governs what an assertion,
257	observation or combination of evidence can establish. The evaluating consumer
258	binds those relations before relying on a reported pass or failure for a broader
259	claim. A supported judgment still supplies no operation or decision mandate.
260	
261	## Orthogonal descriptions
262	
263	Keep three accounts distinct. An algorithmic account specifies the selected
264	transformation. An informational account explains interpreted distinctions and
265	their preservation. A computational account realises the operation through a concrete execution
266	environment: software and hardware, people and communication, or a mixed
267	process, with the effects and resource costs material to its obligations. They are
268	simultaneous descriptions, not successive SDLC stages.
269	
270	To assert a category, specify its domain, objects, typed arrows, arrow equality,
271	identities and associative composition. To assert a functor, define its action
272	on objects and arrows and show identity and composition preservation.
273	For a proposed categorical model, A names the algorithmic account, I the
274	interpreted informational account, and C_H the computational realization on a
275	declared architecture H. They name categories only after the required objects,
276	arrows and laws have been supplied. For a proposed span A -> I and A -> C_H,
277	conformance to Sigma_contract, functorial preservation, semantic equivalence
278	and computational equivalence remain different claims. Categorical
279	equivalence additionally requires the appropriate quasi-inverse and natural
280	isomorphisms on a stated domain; an analogy or matching result is insufficient.
281	
282	Each claimed refinement applies [Preservation obligations](#preservation-obligations)
283	to its declared meaning and any admitted approximation. Each step uses
284	laws valid for its declared subject; without additional laws only universally
285	valid steps are licensed. Laws, records and maps claimed for the method are
286	represented in a_c with premises, consequences and declared choices distinct.
287	The calculus, its interpretation and its carriers retain separate identities.
288	Classify the evidence for each claim as mechanically checked, mathematically
289	argued, tested against an independently specified oracle or unresolved.
290	Structural validation supplies no semantic proof. Claiming the method's
291	categorical construction capability also requires a worked algorithm-to-
292	computation join; an unproved categorical account remains a hypothesis.
293	
294	State sufficiency for a selected decision, statistical Markov properties,
295	conditional independence, a mathematical Markov category and a runtime monad
296	are separate claims. The method neither asserts nor rejects them universally.
297	Their domains, laws and falsifiers must be supplied before using them as proof.
298	
299	## Canonical transformations
300	
301	The [transformation library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) describes Bind, Acquire,
302	Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose. The library defines a shared contract vocabulary with conditional obligations
303	for this selected method domain. Particular methods specialize it through their
304	own types, predicates and authority; it is not six compulsory stages or six
305	runtime APIs. No operation authority follows from a contract definition.
306	A changed detailed determination still returns to its owning contract.
307	
308	## Construction and use
309	
310	The corpus may exceed one actor's capacity. An activation consumes a sufficient
311	projected reference frame and exact subject, with acquisition paths for required
312	material. The projection has declared fidelity and scope; it is not a rival
313	source of authority. Independent evaluation may require overlapping context at
314	a different capability or evidence altitude.
315	
316	Product acceptance, universal mathematical truth, operational efficiency and
317	release each need their own evidence and authority. Shared law supplies deciding
318	obligations within its declared scope; a domain binding supplies its particular
319	predicate and policy. Neither supplies an actor with authority reserved to a
320	named owner.
321	
322	## Result algebra
323	
324	A result makes a claim about one predicate on one subject and basis. Its core
325	record contains the predicate, exact subject and basis, verdict, performance,
326	original qualified domain outcome, supporting evidence and citations, unresolved
327	obligations and material effect observations. A reference can carry these when
328	its resolution preserves their meaning and availability. This is a semantic
329	contract, not a mandatory serialization format or additional work carrier.
330	
331	F1 selects the question and F2/F6 restrict its answer to supported evidence.
332	Because an execution can be interrupted and its effects can outlive its actor
333	(F3/F5), evaluation performance, the predicate's truth and effect completion
334	are separate questions. The informational contribution is the recoverable
335	meaning of each answer; the computational contribution is what was performed
336	and observed. The following value choices implement those distinctions.
337	RF-012 and every domain refinement bind all three questions before consuming a
338	label such as `ready` or `refused`; no label decides the other predicates.
339	
340	The verdict has exactly these values:
341	
342	| Value | Meaning for the bound predicate |
343	|---|---|
344	| `satisfied` | Admissible evidence establishes the predicate under its declared evaluation rule. |
345	| `falsified` | Admissible evidence establishes a counterexample or failure of that predicate. |
346	| `indeterminate` | The available admissible evidence does not decide the predicate. |
347	| `out_of_frame` | The predicate is outside the evaluation's bound scope or capability; it is not silently omitted from the wider obligation. |
348	| `invalid_basis` | The subject, governing basis or required interpretation is invalid for the claimed evaluation. |
349	
350	Performance records whether the named predicate's declared evaluation was
351	actually undertaken; it is `performed`, `not_performed` or `unconfirmed`.
352	The activation identifies that evaluation separately from dispatch, admission
353	or the work being assessed. Retain the observed extent, interruption and
354	conclusion in its outcome and evidence. The legal pairs are:
355	
356	| Performance | Permitted verdicts | Meaning |
357	|---|---|---|
358	| `performed` | Any of the five verdicts | Evidence establishes that the evaluation was undertaken, including a scoped basis or capability diagnosis. Its extent and conclusion remain separate facts. |
359	| `not_performed` | Any except `satisfied`, with the evidence condition below | Evidence establishes that the evaluation was not undertaken. Dispatch or admission alone does not establish performance. |
360	| `unconfirmed` | Any except `satisfied`, with the evidence condition below | Whether the evaluation was undertaken is not established. |
361	
362	An interruption does not erase evaluation already undertaken or admissible
363	evidence obtained. A suite aborted after a witnessed failure is performed with
364	that partial extent and falsifies “all tests pass”. A completed load test that
365	cannot generate its required load is performed but indeterminate on the
366	requested service-performance predicate. Neither case is a never-run test.
367	Satisfaction still requires all evidence and completion conditions selected by
368	the predicate's evaluation rule; performed alone proves none of them.
369	
370	When the selected evaluation was not undertaken or its performance is
371	unconfirmed, separately admissible counterevidence to its bound predicate can
372	still establish falsified; an established basis or scope diagnosis can likewise
373	establish invalid_basis or out_of_frame. The result identifies that independent
374	support without inventing execution. Without deciding support it is
375	indeterminate. An absent return establishes neither non-performance nor an
376	undecidable evaluation: retain the missing slot and what is actually known.
377	
378	A missing required judgment stays an absent coverage slot, with the known
379	performance fact or its uncertainty; it is not a fabricated child result. A
380	performed but undecidable evaluation differs from a known unperformed one and
381	from unconfirmed execution. A failed admission check can conclude while
382	downstream work does not. The plan fixes which predicates are required; a
383	precondition is evidence for its dependent evaluation unless the plan separately
384	requires that precondition as a predicate. A concluding basis/scope diagnosis
385	on P reports invalid_basis/out_of_frame on P with its supporting evidence; a
386	different admission predicate is not silently substituted for P. An aborted
387	procedure does not erase separately authenticated counterexamples observed
388	during the attempt. Every result projection preserves these
389	coordinates and the original predicate; a verdict alone is an insufficient
390	handoff where performance is material.
391	
392	An effect observation is `not_requested`, `not_started`, `completed`, `partial`,
393	`reverted` or `unknown`, on its declared observation boundary. These values describe the selected effect and observation
394	boundary, not the predicate verdict. `not_started` needs evidence that the selected effect did not begin, including
395	an authenticated rejection before mutation. Transport dispatch alone proves
396	neither effect completion nor absence; `unknown` includes a lost acknowledgment
397	after possible execution.
398	`reverted` means that at least one part began and every begun part is observed to have been reversed within
399	the declared boundary, with the reversal and any unstarted remainder retained
400	as evidence. For every effect value, the boundary includes each material part
401	the operation may have affected under its supported operating model and any
402	observed departure, whether requested or unintended. Irreversible messages or
403	other material external effects cannot be omitted to improve a result.
404	`partial` means an observed
405	completed part and an observed requested but unexecuted, or reverted, remainder.
406	If any material remainder has unknown completion, the state is `unknown`,
407	retaining the completed parts as evidence. An effect can be completed while
408	the intended product outcome is falsified.
409	An empty local log or discarded context does not establish no effect.
410	`not_requested` states an established effect-free scope under that operating
411	model; lack of a request alone is insufficient. A material possible unintended
412	effect without sufficient observation is `unknown`. If observation establishes
413	that an unrequested possible part did not begin, it contributes `not_requested`
414	at this boundary, retaining that observation and any earlier uncertainty.
415	It is not an uncompleted requested remainder. A requested part observed not to
416	begin remains `not_started`.
417	
418	A refined value is the pair of original domain outcome and cause in its
419	declared reason domain, including an explicit missing-reason case. A domain
420	refinement preserves that qualified original outcome and supplies a
421	total, reason-sensitive map into this record. If the original outcome is too
422	coarse to determine a verdict, its required reason distinguishes the cases; a
423	consumer cannot guess from a word such as `refused`, `ready` or `accepted`.
424	A missing required reason maps the claimed predicate to indeterminate and
425	leaves that contribution inadmissible as deciding support for its slot;
426	retain its raw outcome and unresolved authentication. Its claimed predicate
427	remains indeterminate until admissible evidence decides it. Independently
428	established counterevidence or a basis/scope diagnosis uses the legal pairs above
429	on that same bound predicate; it does not invent execution or completion.
430	Requested or material possible unintended effects without sufficient observation
431	are unknown, never defaulted to not_requested. Unconfirmed evaluation performance
432	stays unconfirmed. Domain meaning stays with its domain owner.
433	No refinement turns failure, undecidability, non-performance or unknown effect
434	completion into greater standing. A new result over a different predicate does
435	not overwrite the earlier result.
436	
437	Candidate availability, candidate fitness and authorised acceptance are three
438	predicates. `candidate_ready` can satisfy availability while fitness remains
439	falsified or unassessed. A lawful yield can satisfy the selected yielding
440	contract while product completion remains unresolved. A decision result binds
441	the predicate “disposition D on subject S at basis B was made under mandate M
442	by its bound authority”. A lawful rejection can satisfy that predicate while
443	candidate fitness remains undecided. Recording the decision is not its authority.
444	A not-applicable classification needs a supported applicability judgment; it is
445	never a synonym for a missing evaluation.
446	
447	A stop reports the actual destination or task predicate through this record,
448	with its reason, observed effects and outstanding obligations. Its verdict
449	is indeterminate when the outcome remains undecided, falsified when admissible
450	evidence defeats that predicate, or the established scope/basis diagnosis.
451	Lawfulness of stopping is a separate decision predicate.
452	
453	## Result conjunction
454	
455	Conjunction evaluates whether all required predicates and their material joins
456	hold on the declared composite subject and basis. It retains the contributing
457	results, their authentication and predicate mapping, known failures and their
458	citations, uncovered required coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators.
459	The aggregate is another result in the same algebra, with those components
460	available through sufficient references. Its summary never replaces them.
461	
462	The required set comes from the composite's applicability and coverage
463	contract, not from the list of returns received. F4's preservation obligation
464	therefore makes a missing required return visible even when every available
465	return is satisfied. F2/F6 also retain an authenticated counterexample when
466	another slot is missing. Frame conjunction and the library's Conjoin operation
467	apply this same distinction; their owners supply which predicates and joins
468	are required, not another rule for erasing failures or filling gaps.
469	
470	The aggregate evaluation has performance performed when its combining rule is
471	applied; this does not change component performance. The composite declares its
472	effect boundary and the selected effect parts within it. First resolve a current
473	observation for each part, retaining the contributing observations, identities,
474	ordering and any supported supersession. A later timestamp alone is no
475	supersession argument. Conflicting or insufficient observations leave the part
476	unknown. Normalize every material possibly affected part, including one owned
477	by an absent evaluation slot, through the effect-observation rule in
478	[Result algebra](#result-algebra). That rule distinguishes a requested part
479	that did not start from an unrequested possible part observed not to begin.
480	The composite supplies no different classification for either case.
481	
482	Sequential stages can affect the same part. Their local completion labels are
483	not inputs to the composite join until mapped onto that part's observed state
484	at the composite boundary. A completed deployment followed by its completed
485	rollback is reverted for the deployment effect; a subsequent completed
486	reapplication is completed there. The historical rollback remains evidence.
487	The declarations retain every material external part, including irreversible
488	ones; a local reversal cannot silently remove them from the scope.
489	
490	Over the resulting disjoint part observations: any unknown gives unknown;
491	all not_requested gives not_requested; completed with only completed or
492	not_requested gives completed; not_started with only not_started or
493	not_requested gives not_started; reverted with only reverted, not_started or
494	not_requested gives reverted; every remaining fully observed mixture gives
495	partial. Retain each observation's part and contributing components. The combining
496	operation's own lack of mutation cannot label an effectful composite not_requested.
497	
498	First authenticate each contribution against its producer, subject, basis and
499	required plan membership. An unauthenticated claim cannot discharge an
500	obligation. A missing planned judgment remains an absent slot with its known performance
501	fact or uncertainty; required coverage outside an authenticated plan remains
502	uncovered. These are separate
503	conditions. An invalid contribution does not erase an independently
504	authenticated finding.
505	
506	For an interpretable composite predicate and governing basis:
507	
508	1. Any authenticated, applicable falsification of a required predicate or material join makes
509	   the conjunction `falsified`. Missing or undecidable other coverage remains
510	   explicit alongside it.
511	2. With no such falsification, an invalid required basis prevents satisfaction
512	   and yields `invalid_basis`; a required out-of-frame judgment yields
513	   `out_of_frame` when no invalid basis applies.
514	3. Otherwise any unresolved applicability, missing evaluation, undecidable
515	   predicate or undecided material join yields `indeterminate`.
516	4. `satisfied` requires every applicable obligation and material join to be
517	   authentically satisfied, with coverage itself established. An empty list
518	   proves nothing unless the declared required set is established as empty.
519	
520	The composite declaration distinguishes its admission conditions from the
521	material joins of the predicate being evaluated. Each relation has one of
522	those roles in that evaluation. A failed admission condition prevents an
523	interpretation; a false required join is counterevidence within an admitted
524	interpretation. The result names that declared role instead of reclassifying a
525	known failed join as a missing basis. If the composite subject or governing basis itself cannot be interpreted, the
526	aggregate is `invalid_basis`; independently valid component failures and their
527	scope remain exposed. This does not pronounce them false or forgotten.
528	Effect uncertainty prevents satisfaction where the predicate requires a known
529	effect state. An unrelated effect does not automatically invalidate a different
530	predicate; the dependency relation must justify its relevance.
531	
532	A declared operator states its truth and falsity conditions over exact leaf
533	predicates and joins. On its fully decided admitted domain, those conditions
534	are disjoint and exhaustive, including failure of a required join. An
535	overlapping, incomplete or uninterpretable operator declaration is invalid_basis.
536	Unresolved well-formedness makes the operator result indeterminate and supplies
537	neither satisfaction nor falsification; independently valid leaf results remain
538	visible. Once well-formedness is established, its result can be satisfied only when authenticated
539	evidence establishes its truth condition and the material joins and coverage
540	needed for that condition. It can be falsified only on an established falsity
541	condition. Otherwise a material invalid_basis yields invalid_basis, a material
542	out_of_frame yields out_of_frame when no invalid basis applies, and every
543	remaining undecided case is indeterminate. Only dependencies needed to decide
544	the bound predicate enter that ordering. Authentication, original failure
545	retention, performance and effect composition remain the rules above. Negation
546	or disjunction evaluates a different predicate; it cannot erase a failed leaf
547	or pass that result off as conjunction of all leaves. A first-nonfailure rule
548	cannot turn an undecided fallback into success.
549	
550	Sequential composition records an unreturned dependent evaluation as an absent
551	slot, retaining its observed performance, extent and missing conclusion. A lawful regrouping requires the same interpretable composite basis, required
552	leaf predicates, joins, normalized effect parts and authentication, with no intermediate basis failure
553	hidden by the grouping. On that fixed domain, retained component sets combine
554	by union, the conjunction precedence is associative, and the effect join over
555	normalized disjoint parts is associative. The argument is mathematical: union
556	retains the same authenticated leaves under either grouping; selecting the
557	highest applicable diagnostic in the declared precedence over those leaves
558	has the same result. Normalized disjoint effect observations likewise retain
559	the same parts, so the stated unknown and completion conditions decide the same
560	aggregate. An intermediate result must retain those leaves and parts; a bare
561	verdict cannot establish this equivalence. This grants no associativity to an
562	arbitrary declared operator; regrouping it requires preservation of the same
563	outer predicate and its own demonstrated associativity law. An invalid
564	intermediate join is a failed premise of that rewrite, not evidence that every
565	arbitrary grouping is equivalent. Reordering
566	operations additionally needs an effect-independence law; associativity alone
567	supplies no such permission.
568	
569	Sequential operations compose under their applicable owning contracts:
570	[UP-016/017](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#transformation-admission-completeness-stdo-up-016)
571	for design composition and [AC-016](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-016-typed-composition)
572	within a_c. Their returned result applies the operator rule above to the
573	declared outer predicate using
574	its preservation argument and the retained component results. For a pipeline
575	whose contract requires every stage postcondition, this is the conjunction
576	above; a recovery path need not require a failed earlier test to become true.
577	Unexecuted stages remain coverage facts, with no invented evaluations. A
578	sequence without an established outer interpretation or join returns the
579	applicable unresolved or invalid-basis result rather than a guessed success.

represented in a_c with premises, consequences and declared choices distinct.

Classify the evidence for each claim as mechanically checked, mathematically
argued, tested against an independently specified oracle or unresolved.
Structural validation supplies no semantic proof. Claiming the method's
categorical construction capability also requires a worked algorithm-to-
computation join; an unproved categorical account remains a hypothesis.

State sufficiency for a selected decision, statistical Markov properties,
conditional independence, a mathematical Markov category and a runtime monad
are separate claims. The method neither asserts nor rejects them universally.
Their domains, laws and falsifiers must be supplied before using them as proof.

## Canonical transformations

The [transformation library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md) describes Bind, Acquire,
Transform, Evaluate, Conjoin and Dispose. The library defines a shared contract vocabulary with conditional obligations
for this selected method domain. Particular methods specialize it through their
own types, predicates and authority; it is not six compulsory stages or six
runtime APIs. No operation authority follows from a contract definition.
A changed detailed determination still returns to its owning contract.

## Construction and use

The corpus may exceed one actor's capacity. An activation consumes a sufficient
projected reference frame and exact subject, with acquisition paths for required
material. The projection has declared fidelity and scope; it is not a rival
source of authority. Independent evaluation may require overlapping context at
a different capability or evidence altitude.

Product acceptance, universal mathematical truth, operational efficiency and
release each need their own evidence and authority. Shared law supplies deciding
obligations within its declared scope; a domain binding supplies its particular
predicate and policy. Neither supplies an actor with authority reserved to a
named owner.

## Result algebra

A result makes a claim about one predicate on one subject and basis. Its core
record contains the predicate, exact subject and basis, verdict, performance,
original qualified domain outcome, supporting evidence and citations, unresolved
obligations and material effect observations. A reference can carry these when
its resolution preserves their meaning and availability. This is a semantic
contract, not a mandatory serialization format or additional work carrier.

F1 selects the question and F2/F6 restrict its answer to supported evidence.
Because an execution can be interrupted and its effects can outlive its actor
(F3/F5), evaluation performance, the predicate's truth and effect completion
are separate questions. The informational contribution is the recoverable
meaning of each answer; the computational contribution is what was performed
and observed. The following value choices implement those distinctions.
RF-012 and every domain refinement bind all three questions before consuming a
label such as `ready` or `refused`; no label decides the other predicates.

The verdict has exactly these values:

| Value | Meaning for the bound predicate |
|---|---|
| `satisfied` | Admissible evidence establishes the predicate under its declared evaluation rule. |
| `falsified` | Admissible evidence establishes a counterexample or failure of that predicate. |
| `indeterminate` | The available admissible evidence does not decide the predicate. |
| `out_of_frame` | The predicate is outside the evaluation's bound scope or capability; it is not silently omitted from the wider obligation. |
| `invalid_basis` | The subject, governing basis or required interpretation is invalid for the claimed evaluation. |

Performance records whether the named predicate's declared evaluation was
actually undertaken; it is `performed`, `not_performed` or `unconfirmed`.
The activation identifies that evaluation separately from dispatch, admission
or the work being assessed. Retain the observed extent, interruption and
conclusion in its outcome and evidence. The legal pairs are:

| Performance | Permitted verdicts | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `performed` | Any of the five verdicts | Evidence establishes that the evaluation was undertaken, including a scoped basis or capability diagnosis. Its extent and conclusion remain separate facts. |
| `not_performed` | Any except `satisfied`, with the evidence condition below | Evidence establishes that the evaluation was not undertaken. Dispatch or admission alone does not establish performance. |
| `unconfirmed` | Any except `satisfied`, with the evidence condition below | Whether the evaluation was undertaken is not established. |

An interruption does not erase evaluation already undertaken or admissible
evidence obtained. A suite aborted after a witnessed failure is performed with
that partial extent and falsifies “all tests pass”. A completed load test that
cannot generate its required load is performed but indeterminate on the
requested service-performance predicate. Neither case is a never-run test.
Satisfaction still requires all evidence and completion conditions selected by
the predicate's evaluation rule; performed alone proves none of them.

When the selected evaluation was not undertaken or its performance is
unconfirmed, separately admissible counterevidence to its bound predicate can
still establish falsified; an established basis or scope diagnosis can likewise
establish invalid_basis or out_of_frame. The result identifies that independent
support without inventing execution. Without deciding support it is
indeterminate. An absent return establishes neither non-performance nor an
undecidable evaluation: retain the missing slot and what is actually known.

A missing required judgment stays an absent coverage slot, with the known
performance fact or its uncertainty; it is not a fabricated child result. A
performed but undecidable evaluation differs from a known unperformed one and
from unconfirmed execution. A failed admission check can conclude while
downstream work does not. The plan fixes which predicates are required; a
precondition is evidence for its dependent evaluation unless the plan separately
requires that precondition as a predicate. A concluding basis/scope diagnosis
on P reports invalid_basis/out_of_frame on P with its supporting evidence; a
different admission predicate is not silently substituted for P. An aborted
procedure does not erase separately authenticated counterexamples observed
during the attempt. Every result projection preserves these
coordinates and the original predicate; a verdict alone is an insufficient
handoff where performance is material.

An effect observation is `not_requested`, `not_started`, `completed`, `partial`,
`reverted` or `unknown`, on its declared observation boundary. These values describe the selected effect and observation
boundary, not the predicate verdict. `not_started` needs evidence that the selected effect did not begin, including
an authenticated rejection before mutation. Transport dispatch alone proves
neither effect completion nor absence; `unknown` includes a lost acknowledgment
after possible execution.
`reverted` means that at least one part began and every begun part is observed to have been reversed within
the declared boundary, with the reversal and any unstarted remainder retained
as evidence. For every effect value, the boundary includes each material part
the operation may have affected under its supported operating model and any
observed departure, whether requested or unintended. Irreversible messages or
other material external effects cannot be omitted to improve a result.
`partial` means an observed
completed part and an observed requested but unexecuted, or reverted, remainder.
If any material remainder has unknown completion, the state is `unknown`,
retaining the completed parts as evidence. An effect can be completed while
the intended product outcome is falsified.
An empty local log or discarded context does not establish no effect.
`not_requested` states an established effect-free scope under that operating
model; lack of a request alone is insufficient. A material possible unintended
effect without sufficient observation is `unknown`. If observation establishes
that an unrequested possible part did not begin, it contributes `not_requested`
at this boundary, retaining that observation and any earlier uncertainty.
It is not an uncompleted requested remainder. A requested part observed not to
begin remains `not_started`.

A refined value is the pair of original domain outcome and cause in its
declared reason domain, including an explicit missing-reason case. A domain
refinement preserves that qualified original outcome and supplies a
total, reason-sensitive map into this record. If the original outcome is too
coarse to determine a verdict, its required reason distinguishes the cases; a
consumer cannot guess from a word such as `refused`, `ready` or `accepted`.
A missing required reason maps the claimed predicate to indeterminate and
leaves that contribution inadmissible as deciding support for its slot;
retain its raw outcome and unresolved authentication. Its claimed predicate
remains indeterminate until admissible evidence decides it. Independently
established counterevidence or a basis/scope diagnosis uses the legal pairs above
on that same bound predicate; it does not invent execution or completion.
Requested or material possible unintended effects without sufficient observation
are unknown, never defaulted to not_requested. Unconfirmed evaluation performance
stays unconfirmed. Domain meaning stays with its domain owner.
No refinement turns failure, undecidability, non-performance or unknown effect
completion into greater standing. A new result over a different predicate does
not overwrite the earlier result.

Candidate availability, candidate fitness and authorised acceptance are three
predicates. `candidate_ready` can satisfy availability while fitness remains
falsified or unassessed. A lawful yield can satisfy the selected yielding
contract while product completion remains unresolved. A decision result binds
the predicate “disposition D on subject S at basis B was made under mandate M
by its bound authority”. A lawful rejection can satisfy that predicate while
candidate fitness remains undecided. Recording the decision is not its authority.
A not-applicable classification needs a supported applicability judgment; it is
never a synonym for a missing evaluation.

A stop reports the actual destination or task predicate through this record,
with its reason, observed effects and outstanding obligations. Its verdict
is indeterminate when the outcome remains undecided, falsified when admissible
evidence defeats that predicate, or the established scope/basis diagnosis.
Lawfulness of stopping is a separate decision predicate.

## Result conjunction

Conjunction evaluates whether all required predicates and their material joins
hold on the declared composite subject and basis. It retains the contributing
results, their authentication and predicate mapping, known failures and their
citations, uncovered required coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators.
The aggregate is another result in the same algebra, with those components
available through sufficient references. Its summary never replaces them.

The required set comes from the composite's applicability and coverage
contract, not from the list of returns received. F4's preservation obligation
therefore makes a missing required return visible even when every available
return is satisfied. F2/F6 also retain an authenticated counterexample when
another slot is missing. Frame conjunction and the library's Conjoin operation
apply this same distinction; their owners supply which predicates and joins
are required, not another rule for erasing failures or filling gaps.

The aggregate evaluation has performance performed when its combining rule is
applied; this does not change component performance. The composite declares its
effect boundary and the selected effect parts within it. First resolve a current
observation for each part, retaining the contributing observations, identities,
ordering and any supported supersession. A later timestamp alone is no
supersession argument. Conflicting or insufficient observations leave the part
unknown. Normalize every material possibly affected part, including one owned
by an absent evaluation slot, through the effect-observation rule in
[Result algebra](#result-algebra). That rule distinguishes a requested part
that did not start from an unrequested possible part observed not to begin.
The composite supplies no different classification for either case.

Sequential stages can affect the same part. Their local completion labels are
not inputs to the composite join until mapped onto that part's observed state
at the composite boundary. A completed deployment followed by its completed
rollback is reverted for the deployment effect; a subsequent completed
reapplication is completed there. The historical rollback remains evidence.
The declarations retain every material external part, including irreversible
ones; a local reversal cannot silently remove them from the scope.

Over the resulting disjoint part observations: any unknown gives unknown;
all not_requested gives not_requested; completed with only completed or
not_requested gives completed; not_started with only not_started or
not_requested gives not_started; reverted with only reverted, not_started or
not_requested gives reverted; every remaining fully observed mixture gives
partial. Retain each observation's part and contributing components. The combining
operation's own lack of mutation cannot label an effectful composite not_requested.

First authenticate each contribution against its producer, subject, basis and
required plan membership. An unauthenticated claim cannot discharge an
obligation. A missing planned judgment remains an absent slot with its known performance
fact or uncertainty; required coverage outside an authenticated plan remains
uncovered. These are separate
conditions. An invalid contribution does not erase an independently
authenticated finding.

For an interpretable composite predicate and governing basis:

1. Any authenticated, applicable falsification of a required predicate or material join makes
   the conjunction `falsified`. Missing or undecidable other coverage remains
   explicit alongside it.
2. With no such falsification, an invalid required basis prevents satisfaction
   and yields `invalid_basis`; a required out-of-frame judgment yields
   `out_of_frame` when no invalid basis applies.
3. Otherwise any unresolved applicability, missing evaluation, undecidable
   predicate or undecided material join yields `indeterminate`.
4. `satisfied` requires every applicable obligation and material join to be
   authentically satisfied, with coverage itself established. An empty list
   proves nothing unless the declared required set is established as empty.

The composite declaration distinguishes its admission conditions from the
material joins of the predicate being evaluated. Each relation has one of
those roles in that evaluation. A failed admission condition prevents an
interpretation; a false required join is counterevidence within an admitted
interpretation. The result names that declared role instead of reclassifying a
known failed join as a missing basis. If the composite subject or governing basis itself cannot be interpreted, the
aggregate is `invalid_basis`; independently valid component failures and their
scope remain exposed. This does not pronounce them false or forgotten.
Effect uncertainty prevents satisfaction where the predicate requires a known
effect state. An unrelated effect does not automatically invalidate a different
predicate; the dependency relation must justify its relevance.

A declared operator states its truth and falsity conditions over exact leaf
predicates and joins. On its fully decided admitted domain, those conditions
are disjoint and exhaustive, including failure of a required join. An
overlapping, incomplete or uninterpretable operator declaration is invalid_basis.
Unresolved well-formedness makes the operator result indeterminate and supplies
neither satisfaction nor falsification; independently valid leaf results remain
visible. Once well-formedness is established, its result can be satisfied only when authenticated
evidence establishes its truth condition and the material joins and coverage
needed for that condition. It can be falsified only on an established falsity
condition. Otherwise a material invalid_basis yields invalid_basis, a material
out_of_frame yields out_of_frame when no invalid basis applies, and every
remaining undecided case is indeterminate. Only dependencies needed to decide
the bound predicate enter that ordering. Authentication, original failure
retention, performance and effect composition remain the rules above. Negation
or disjunction evaluates a different predicate; it cannot erase a failed leaf
or pass that result off as conjunction of all leaves. A first-nonfailure rule
cannot turn an undecided fallback into success.

Sequential composition records an unreturned dependent evaluation as an absent
slot, retaining its observed performance, extent and missing conclusion. A lawful regrouping requires the same interpretable composite basis, required
leaf predicates, joins, normalized effect parts and authentication, with no intermediate basis failure
hidden by the grouping. On that fixed domain, retained component sets combine
by union, the conjunction precedence is associative, and the effect join over
normalized disjoint parts is associative. The argument is mathematical: union
retains the same authenticated leaves under either grouping; selecting the
highest applicable diagnostic in the declared precedence over those leaves
has the same result. Normalized disjoint effect observations likewise retain
the same parts, so the stated unknown and completion conditions decide the same
aggregate. An intermediate result must retain those leaves and parts; a bare
verdict cannot establish this equivalence. This grants no associativity to an
arbitrary declared operator; regrouping it requires preservation of the same
outer predicate and its own demonstrated associativity law. An invalid
intermediate join is a failed premise of that rewrite, not evidence that every
arbitrary grouping is equivalent. Reordering
operations additionally needs an effect-independence law; associativity alone
supplies no such permission.

Sequential operations compose under their applicable owning contracts:
[UP-016/017](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#transformation-admission-completeness-stdo-up-016)
for design composition and [AC-016](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-016-typed-composition)
within a_c. Their returned result applies the operator rule above to the
declared outer predicate using
its preservation argument and the retained component results. For a pipeline
whose contract requires every stage postcondition, this is the conjunction
above; a recovery path need not require a failed earlier test to become true.
Unexecuted stages remain coverage facts, with no invented evaluations. A
sequence without an established outer interpretation or join returns the
applicable unresolved or invalid-basis result rather than a guessed success.

1215	## Ambiguity Governance Rule
1216	
1217	Given F1, F2, F5 and F6 and a material unresolved interpretation, unsupported
1218	meaning cannot become an established result or permission. Apply
1219	[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) to the
1220	affected claim. This family chooses mandatory detection, lifecycle sufficiency
1221	and the hard stops below; the Product's declared risk policy separately chooses
1222	which remaining ambiguities may be carried, resolved or escalated.
1223	
1224	`SPEC_METHOD.md` owns the substrate-neutral ambiguity-governance bounded
1225	context `urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance` under the selected
1226	complete STDO basis. Graph/runtime shorthands such as `F_D`, `F_P`, and `F_H`
1227	remain in the graph-native ODD context unless an explicit relation imports or
1228	translates them.
1229	
1230	Spec-driven development is not only a derivation pipeline. It is a governed
1231	disambiguation pipeline.
1232	
1233	The point of the upstream chain is to progressively reduce ambiguity:
1234	
1235	- goals narrow active priority and work-wave focus
1236	- intent narrows direction and scope
1237	- product narrows current realization shape and terms
1238	- requirements narrow constitutional obligation
1239	- build-tenant or stack choice narrows executable realization class
1240	- design narrows structural interpretation
1241	- implementation narrows local realization detail
1242	
1243	This narrowing is not uniform. The methodology distinguishes between:
1244	
1245	- **major ambiguity**: ambiguity that materially changes architecture, stack,
1246	  product boundary, execution/deployment admissibility, public contract shape,
1247	  or other downstream realization law
1248	- **micro ambiguity**: local implementation choice that remains inside an
1249	  already-governed design boundary
1250	
1251	Major ambiguity must always be surfaced and governed. It may not remain hidden
1252	inside informal operator judgment, ambient precedent, or silent model choice.
1253	
1254	Therefore, at each major boundary the process must:
1255	
1256	- detect and record the major ambiguity that remains or is newly introduced
1257	- identify the affected invariant, asset, or decision boundary
1258	- record the decision taken if work proceeds
1259	- record whether the ambiguity was resolved, carried forward, escalated, or
1260	  blocked
1261	
1262	Ambiguity detection is mandatory. Blocking is policy.
1263	
1264	**Lawful Probabilistic Processing**
1265	(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing`) is
1266	bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or resolve
1267	declared ambiguity. **Human Adjudication**
1268	(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication`) is explicit human
1269	judgment admitted by authority to resolve declared ambiguity where policy or
1270	risk appetite requires it.
1271	
1272	The default governance model is:
1273	
1274	- ambiguity may be carried or decided by lawful probabilistic processing when
1275	  project policy allows it
1276	- ambiguity may be escalated to explicit human adjudication when project policy
1277	  requires it
1278	- the threshold between those actions is determined by declared risk appetite,
1279	  not by silent convenience
1280	
1281	Projects may therefore choose different ambiguity-handling policies. A lower
1282	risk appetite escalates more major ambiguity to explicit human judgment. A
1283	higher risk appetite permits more bounded probabilistic decision-making. In either
1284	case, the ambiguity and the decision must be recorded.
1285	
1286	`Resolved`, `carried forward`, `escalated` and `blocked` record handling, not four
1287	verdicts on the affected Product claim. Evaluate `the identified ambiguity is
1288	resolved under its governing meaning`: established resolution is `satisfied`,
1289	an established remaining ambiguity is `falsified`, and insufficient evidence is
1290	`indeterminate`, retaining applicable `invalid_basis` or `out_of_frame`
1291	diagnoses. A carried or escalated ambiguity may still be unresolved. Separately,
1292	the core decision predicate evaluates whether the recorded handling was made
1293	under the bound policy and authority: supported lawful handling is `satisfied`,
1294	a demonstrated violation is `falsified`, and unsupported handling is
1295	`indeterminate`, subject to the same basis/scope diagnoses. Neither result
1296	settles delivery or grants authority outside that policy.
1297	
1298	Some conditions are not optional ambiguity decisions and therefore remain hard
1299	stops regardless of risk appetite. Typical hard-stop classes include:
1300	
1301	- violated invariant or guarantee
1302	- absent required authority surface
1303	- missing declared capability for an executional or operational stage
1304	- undeclared irreversible side effect
1305	- explicit policy gate requiring human approval
1306	
1307	A hard stop returns the affected task predicate through the
1308	[core stop rule](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra). A witnessed invariant violation
1309	or unmet required authorization falsifies the corresponding admissibility
1310	predicate; missing evidence about that condition leaves it indeterminate.
1311	Admissibility and fulfillment of the interrupted task remain separate
1312	predicates: refusal alone does not establish that the intended outcome failed.
1313	An unusable governing
1314	basis or an evaluation outside capability retains its own diagnosis. The stop
1315	label proves neither non-performance nor absence of effects; an undeclared or
1316	uncertain effect needs actual observation before dependent action.
1317	
1318	The methodology is therefore not "eliminate all ambiguity before work." It is
1319	"make ambiguity visible, govern it explicitly, and reduce it progressively until
1320	downstream realization is sufficiently constrained."

## Ambiguity Governance Rule

Given F1, F2, F5 and F6 and a material unresolved interpretation, unsupported
meaning cannot become an established result or permission. Apply
[Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application) to the
affected claim. This family chooses mandatory detection, lifecycle sufficiency
and the hard stops below; the Product's declared risk policy separately chooses
which remaining ambiguities may be carried, resolved or escalated.

`SPEC_METHOD.md` owns the substrate-neutral ambiguity-governance bounded
context `urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance` under the selected
complete STDO basis. Graph/runtime shorthands such as `F_D`, `F_P`, and `F_H`
remain in the graph-native ODD context unless an explicit relation imports or
translates them.

Spec-driven development is not only a derivation pipeline. It is a governed
disambiguation pipeline.

The point of the upstream chain is to progressively reduce ambiguity:

- goals narrow active priority and work-wave focus
- intent narrows direction and scope
- product narrows current realization shape and terms
- requirements narrow constitutional obligation
- build-tenant or stack choice narrows executable realization class
- design narrows structural interpretation
- implementation narrows local realization detail

This narrowing is not uniform. The methodology distinguishes between:

- **major ambiguity**: ambiguity that materially changes architecture, stack,
  product boundary, execution/deployment admissibility, public contract shape,
  or other downstream realization law
- **micro ambiguity**: local implementation choice that remains inside an
  already-governed design boundary

Major ambiguity must always be surfaced and governed. It may not remain hidden
inside informal operator judgment, ambient precedent, or silent model choice.

Therefore, at each major boundary the process must:

- detect and record the major ambiguity that remains or is newly introduced
- identify the affected invariant, asset, or decision boundary
- record the decision taken if work proceeds
- record whether the ambiguity was resolved, carried forward, escalated, or
  blocked

Ambiguity detection is mandatory. Blocking is policy.

**Lawful Probabilistic Processing**
(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing`) is
bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or resolve
declared ambiguity. **Human Adjudication**
(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication`) is explicit human
judgment admitted by authority to resolve declared ambiguity where policy or
risk appetite requires it.

The default governance model is:

- ambiguity may be carried or decided by lawful probabilistic processing when
  project policy allows it
- ambiguity may be escalated to explicit human adjudication when project policy
  requires it
- the threshold between those actions is determined by declared risk appetite,
  not by silent convenience

Projects may therefore choose different ambiguity-handling policies. A lower
risk appetite escalates more major ambiguity to explicit human judgment. A
higher risk appetite permits more bounded probabilistic decision-making. In either
case, the ambiguity and the decision must be recorded.

`Resolved`, `carried forward`, `escalated` and `blocked` record handling, not four
verdicts on the affected Product claim. Evaluate `the identified ambiguity is
resolved under its governing meaning`: established resolution is `satisfied`,
an established remaining ambiguity is `falsified`, and insufficient evidence is
`indeterminate`, retaining applicable `invalid_basis` or `out_of_frame`
diagnoses. A carried or escalated ambiguity may still be unresolved. Separately,
the core decision predicate evaluates whether the recorded handling was made
under the bound policy and authority: supported lawful handling is `satisfied`,
a demonstrated violation is `falsified`, and unsupported handling is
`indeterminate`, subject to the same basis/scope diagnoses. Neither result
settles delivery or grants authority outside that policy.

Some conditions are not optional ambiguity decisions and therefore remain hard
stops regardless of risk appetite. Typical hard-stop classes include:

- violated invariant or guarantee
- absent required authority surface
- missing declared capability for an executional or operational stage
- undeclared irreversible side effect
- explicit policy gate requiring human approval

A hard stop returns the affected task predicate through the
[core stop rule](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra). A witnessed invariant violation
or unmet required authorization falsifies the corresponding admissibility
predicate; missing evidence about that condition leaves it indeterminate.
Admissibility and fulfillment of the interrupted task remain separate
predicates: refusal alone does not establish that the intended outcome failed.
An unusable governing
basis or an evaluation outside capability retains its own diagnosis. The stop
label proves neither non-performance nor absence of effects; an undeclared or
uncertain effect needs actual observation before dependent action.

The methodology is therefore not "eliminate all ambiguity before work." It is
"make ambiguity visible, govern it explicitly, and reduce it progressively until
downstream realization is sufficiently constrained."

---

1	# Ticket Method
2	
3	This work-carrier member binds the shared [transformation library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md)
4	to durable work identity, admission, recording and closure. Given finite actor
5	context and obligations that may outlive it, continuing work needs a recoverable
6	source independent of private memory. The
7	[workspace/context relation](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) supplies that
8	requirement; Work-Carrier-To-Execution chooses the smallest carrier for its
9	actual lifetime. Tickets, sprints and the default file layout are this member's
10	additional policy, not universal consequences of finite capacity. Admission and
11	closure consume the shared [result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) and
12	[conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction) at their deciding boundaries.
13	The bindings below preserve core performance, coverage, diagnostic precedence
14	and actual effects. They add no evaluation pass or record to the existing work.
15	
16	## Carrier Families
17	
18	These arguments apply the adopted [F1–F6 commitments](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments)
19	to work whose authority, lifetime and completion conditions are already bound.
20	Their pillar contributions explain different carrier decisions; durable
21	recording, execution admission and acceptance do not follow from the same
22	premise. The linked consumers own the actual policies and their exceptions.
23	
24	| Deciding consumer | Premises and pillar contribution | Consequence at that consumer | Additional policy and owner |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| [Work-Carrier-To-Execution Rule](#work-carrier-to-execution-rule) and [Core Model](#core-model) | F1, F3 and F5; work or an obligation may survive its current actor, run or batch. Reference frames bound private context; persistent identity and state let a later actor resume the same obligation. | If continuation needs a fact or open obligation after the local boundary, private memory cannot be its only carrier. The carrier must preserve the state needed for that continuation. This premise does not require a durable ticket when no independent state survives. | Ticket chooses one run-scoped contract, the ordered ticket/sprint/run selection table and the durable result surface. The Product Definition locates carriers; ticket-state authority decides permitted durable-ticket mutations. |
27	| [Execution Contract Admission](#execution-contract-admission) | F2, F3 and F6; a proposed contract cites upstream work authority and an admission mechanism. Specification and project structure bind that authority; evidence distinguishes a checked contract from a record that merely claims admission. | The presence of a ticket, an active lane or an admission label cannot prove that the cited grant covers the exact work. Admission must concern that contract under that basis; successful admission still does not perform the work or renew its outcome authority. | Ticket chooses deterministic admission or an exact human override, required contract fields and admission states. The Product-bound mechanism admits the contract; the Goals/work-wave owner admits or renews its growth basis. |
28	| [Authority](#authority), [One-Truth State Projection And Drift Refusal](#one-truth-state-projection-and-drift-refusal-stdo-up-009) and [Milestone And Phase-Scoped Truth](#milestone-and-phase-scoped-truth-stdo-up-006) | F2, F3 and F6; goals, tickets, milestones, boards and comments can describe different claims about apparently the same work. Information fidelity preserves each claim's subject and authority through projection. | A board's green label cannot replace the ticket's state, and a milestone's acceptance establishes only its own bounded claim. Divergent projections require resolution at their owning sources before relying on the affected closure claim. | Ticket chooses the work-wave, ticket and milestone authority split, minimum status sets and default layout. The Product binding permits explicit carrier rebinding; comments retain the standing owned by Posting Guide. |
29	| [Sprint Compliance Escrow](#sprint-compliance-escrow) and [Sprint Close Review](#sprint-close-review) | F1, F4–F6; admitted work may defer local proof inside a bounded batch. Concrete execution costs motivate batching; algebraic conservation keeps deferred obligations in the batch's closing claim. | Deferral changes the time at which permitted proof is supplied, not whether it is owed. Closing a sprint therefore cannot erase debt merely because its iterations stopped. Law-changing work still needs its own re-entry rather than a larger escrow. | Ticket chooses manifests, escrow fields, close classifications and durable follow-up. Spec owns the sprint boundary; governing law decides what debt may be deferred or carried beyond close. |
30	| [Multi-Build-Tenant Ticket Independence](#multi-build-tenant-ticket-independence) and [Multi-Build-Tenant Review Rule](#multi-build-tenant-review-rule) | F2, F3 and F6; one common WHAT has more than one independently realized HOW. Specification structure distinguishes the realization subjects; identity binds proof to the tenant actually examined. | Proof or acceptance of one tenant's realization establishes no other tenant's lifecycle result. Shared requirements or a shared issue title cannot hide a peer blocker or transfer closure. | Ticket chooses tenant-local records and the source-ticket/build-tenant fields. The Product's tenant registry owns tenant identity; each tenant's governing work authority owns its lifecycle decisions. |
31	| [Recorded Judgment And Owner-Ruling Continuity](#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity), [Condition-Based Closure And Reuse](#condition-based-closure-and-reuse) and [Test Case Authority](#test-case-authority) | F1–F6; work has declared completion and non-closure conditions, some requiring particular owner decisions, and its support can outlive an actor. Algebraic conjunction preserves every applicable obligation; evidence and authority distinguish an assessment from the required decision. | Closure needs evidence on those exact predicates. A lawful rejection cannot satisfy a predicate requiring acceptance; a completed review cannot replace an absent condition. A recorded judgment remains usable when its support is current, so a new actor alone supplies no reason to repeat it. | Ticket chooses closure-bearing fields, judgment/ruling continuity and test-authority reconciliation. Foundations owns currentness and conjunction. The applicable law selects independent review and reserved acceptance; it does not create an extra review where neither applies. |
32	| [Bounded-Context Term Binding](#bounded-context-term-binding) and [Upward Propagation Check](#upward-propagation-check) | F1–F3 and F6; a work description uses terms whose meanings and governing layers may differ from their familiar spelling. Information and interpretation bind the exact meaning; correction follows the layer found insufficient. | An unresolved material term cannot support admission or closure by familiarity. A familiar implementation file cannot determine re-entry when the actual gap lies in a requirement or Product relation. | Spec owns semantic resolution and lawful change classes. Ticket chooses the work fields, relation references and upward propagation check that carry the classification and unresolved scope. |
33	| [Implementation Migration Category](#implementation-migration-category), [Migration Strategy Requirements](#migration-strategy-requirements) and [Mixed-State Negative Proof](#mixed-state-negative-proof) | F2–F4 and F6; a migration replaces an authoritative relation across producers, consumers and proofs. Functional design supplies the composed interfaces; identity and conservation preserve the declared affected scope. | A green wrapper or mixed old/new proof cannot establish that the new authority path governs the claimed scope. Closure needs evidence of the required replacement and the disposition of the old path; a downstream result cannot silently supply its missing source-carrier condition. | Ticket chooses migration declarations, strategy values, break-to-closure records and follow-up. Spec owns migration policy and its affected-path limits; the owning work authority selects optional extensions. |
34	
35	## Core Model
36	
37	This carrier family assumes [F1, F3, F5 and F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments)
38	and work whose obligations may survive an activation. Continued reliance then
39	requires recoverable identity, state and authority under
40	[workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context). This member
41	chooses Goals, tickets, sprints, run contracts, the smallest-carrier rule and
42	UP-006 milestone truth. Product and ticket-state authorities select their
43	bindings; filenames and lifecycle states do not create execution or acceptance
44	authority. UP-006 applies core conjunction to closure-bearing milestone claims
45	without merging their scopes or treating deferred work as delivered.

# Ticket Method

This work-carrier member binds the shared [transformation library](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md)
to durable work identity, admission, recording and closure. Given finite actor
context and obligations that may outlive it, continuing work needs a recoverable
source independent of private memory. The
[workspace/context relation](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) supplies that
requirement; Work-Carrier-To-Execution chooses the smallest carrier for its
actual lifetime. Tickets, sprints and the default file layout are this member's
additional policy, not universal consequences of finite capacity. Admission and
closure consume the shared [result algebra](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) and
[conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-conjunction) at their deciding boundaries.
The bindings below preserve core performance, coverage, diagnostic precedence
and actual effects. They add no evaluation pass or record to the existing work.

## Carrier Families

These arguments apply the adopted [F1–F6 commitments](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments)
to work whose authority, lifetime and completion conditions are already bound.
Their pillar contributions explain different carrier decisions; durable
recording, execution admission and acceptance do not follow from the same
premise. The linked consumers own the actual policies and their exceptions.

| Deciding consumer | Premises and pillar contribution | Consequence at that consumer | Additional policy and owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Work-Carrier-To-Execution Rule](#work-carrier-to-execution-rule) and [Core Model](#core-model) | F1, F3 and F5; work or an obligation may survive its current actor, run or batch. Reference frames bound private context; persistent identity and state let a later actor resume the same obligation. | If continuation needs a fact or open obligation after the local boundary, private memory cannot be its only carrier. The carrier must preserve the state needed for that continuation. This premise does not require a durable ticket when no independent state survives. | Ticket chooses one run-scoped contract, the ordered ticket/sprint/run selection table and the durable result surface. The Product Definition locates carriers; ticket-state authority decides permitted durable-ticket mutations. |
| [Execution Contract Admission](#execution-contract-admission) | F2, F3 and F6; a proposed contract cites upstream work authority and an admission mechanism. Specification and project structure bind that authority; evidence distinguishes a checked contract from a record that merely claims admission. | The presence of a ticket, an active lane or an admission label cannot prove that the cited grant covers the exact work. Admission must concern that contract under that basis; successful admission still does not perform the work or renew its outcome authority. | Ticket chooses deterministic admission or an exact human override, required contract fields and admission states. The Product-bound mechanism admits the contract; the Goals/work-wave owner admits or renews its growth basis. |
| [Authority](#authority), [One-Truth State Projection And Drift Refusal](#one-truth-state-projection-and-drift-refusal-stdo-up-009) and [Milestone And Phase-Scoped Truth](#milestone-and-phase-scoped-truth-stdo-up-006) | F2, F3 and F6; goals, tickets, milestones, boards and comments can describe different claims about apparently the same work. Information fidelity preserves each claim's subject and authority through projection. | A board's green label cannot replace the ticket's state, and a milestone's acceptance establishes only its own bounded claim. Divergent projections require resolution at their owning sources before relying on the affected closure claim. | Ticket chooses the work-wave, ticket and milestone authority split, minimum status sets and default layout. The Product binding permits explicit carrier rebinding; comments retain the standing owned by Posting Guide. |
| [Sprint Compliance Escrow](#sprint-compliance-escrow) and [Sprint Close Review](#sprint-close-review) | F1, F4–F6; admitted work may defer local proof inside a bounded batch. Concrete execution costs motivate batching; algebraic conservation keeps deferred obligations in the batch's closing claim. | Deferral changes the time at which permitted proof is supplied, not whether it is owed. Closing a sprint therefore cannot erase debt merely because its iterations stopped. Law-changing work still needs its own re-entry rather than a larger escrow. | Ticket chooses manifests, escrow fields, close classifications and durable follow-up. Spec owns the sprint boundary; governing law decides what debt may be deferred or carried beyond close. |
| [Multi-Build-Tenant Ticket Independence](#multi-build-tenant-ticket-independence) and [Multi-Build-Tenant Review Rule](#multi-build-tenant-review-rule) | F2, F3 and F6; one common WHAT has more than one independently realized HOW. Specification structure distinguishes the realization subjects; identity binds proof to the tenant actually examined. | Proof or acceptance of one tenant's realization establishes no other tenant's lifecycle result. Shared requirements or a shared issue title cannot hide a peer blocker or transfer closure. | Ticket chooses tenant-local records and the source-ticket/build-tenant fields. The Product's tenant registry owns tenant identity; each tenant's governing work authority owns its lifecycle decisions. |
| [Recorded Judgment And Owner-Ruling Continuity](#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity), [Condition-Based Closure And Reuse](#condition-based-closure-and-reuse) and [Test Case Authority](#test-case-authority) | F1–F6; work has declared completion and non-closure conditions, some requiring particular owner decisions, and its support can outlive an actor. Algebraic conjunction preserves every applicable obligation; evidence and authority distinguish an assessment from the required decision. | Closure needs evidence on those exact predicates. A lawful rejection cannot satisfy a predicate requiring acceptance; a completed review cannot replace an absent condition. A recorded judgment remains usable when its support is current, so a new actor alone supplies no reason to repeat it. | Ticket chooses closure-bearing fields, judgment/ruling continuity and test-authority reconciliation. Foundations owns currentness and conjunction. The applicable law selects independent review and reserved acceptance; it does not create an extra review where neither applies. |
| [Bounded-Context Term Binding](#bounded-context-term-binding) and [Upward Propagation Check](#upward-propagation-check) | F1–F3 and F6; a work description uses terms whose meanings and governing layers may differ from their familiar spelling. Information and interpretation bind the exact meaning; correction follows the layer found insufficient. | An unresolved material term cannot support admission or closure by familiarity. A familiar implementation file cannot determine re-entry when the actual gap lies in a requirement or Product relation. | Spec owns semantic resolution and lawful change classes. Ticket chooses the work fields, relation references and upward propagation check that carry the classification and unresolved scope. |
| [Implementation Migration Category](#implementation-migration-category), [Migration Strategy Requirements](#migration-strategy-requirements) and [Mixed-State Negative Proof](#mixed-state-negative-proof) | F2–F4 and F6; a migration replaces an authoritative relation across producers, consumers and proofs. Functional design supplies the composed interfaces; identity and conservation preserve the declared affected scope. | A green wrapper or mixed old/new proof cannot establish that the new authority path governs the claimed scope. Closure needs evidence of the required replacement and the disposition of the old path; a downstream result cannot silently supply its missing source-carrier condition. | Ticket chooses migration declarations, strategy values, break-to-closure records and follow-up. Spec owns migration policy and its affected-path limits; the owning work authority selects optional extensions. |

## Core Model

This carrier family assumes [F1, F3, F5 and F6](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundational-commitments)
and work whose obligations may survive an activation. Continued reliance then
requires recoverable identity, state and authority under
[workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context). This member
chooses Goals, tickets, sprints, run contracts, the smallest-carrier rule and
UP-006 milestone truth. Product and ticket-state authorities select their
bindings; filenames and lifecycle states do not create execution or acceptance
authority. UP-006 applies core conjunction to closure-bearing milestone claims
without merging their scopes or treating deferred work as delivered.
